page: Amazon Web Services m7i.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8488C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions and Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with high ratings in single-threaded gzip compression, Geekbench single-core execution, and text processing. However, multi-core scaling presents a notable tradeoff; the instance exhibits weaker performance in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation tasks. Memory performance is mixed, showing average bandwidth for cached small-block reads and large-block writes, but dropping to a weaker tier for uncached large-block reads.

The m7i.xlarge does not include local NVMe storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and strong single-core capabilities, this instance is suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, basic text processing, and light LLM inference tasks using small models. It is less optimal for memory-bound database operations or highly parallelized multi-threaded compilation tasks due to its lower multi-core and uncached memory read performance.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8488C processor. Operating at 3.2 GHz, it features 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory. The processor supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, particularly in text processing and single-threaded gzip compression. However, multi-core performance and uncached large-block memory reads are relatively weak. Lacking local storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for balanced workloads that do not require heavy parallelization. It is best suited for static web serving, light text processing, and small-scale model inference, while being less optimal for database operations or multi-threaded compilation.
